afterTaps()

The afterTaps() method registers observational callbacks on a FeatureCell that execute immediately after reducer execution. After taps provide a controlled extension point for observing committed pipeline values and performing side effects without influencing state computation or pipeline flow.

Method Contract Summary

  • After Tap behaviors are registered declaratively on a FeatureCell instance
  • Callbacks execute after reducer execution
  • Callbacks receive an immutable resolved pipeline value
  • Callbacks must not mutate state or return values
  • Errors propagate as Vault errors

The afterTaps() method defines observation and side effects only. It does not modify state, alter pipeline execution, suppress snapshots, or participate in value derivation. Its responsibility is limited to attaching post-reduction observers to the FeatureCell runtime surface.

Note

The afterTaps() method is additive. It may be invoked multiple times, and each call appends callbacks to the FeatureCell’s after-tap callback list. Callbacks may be supplied as a single array or across multiple method invocations; in all cases, after taps execute in the exact order they are registered during initialization.

While multiple invocations are supported, the recommended practice is to register related after tap callbacks as a single ordered array to preserve clarity and intentional execution ordering.

Registers one or more tap callbacks executed during the After Tap stage of the pipeline. Callbacks observe the resolved pipeline value immediately after reducer execution and may perform side effects without mutating state or influencing pipeline control flow.
Example

The afterTaps() method registers one or more tap callbacks that execute immediately after reducer execution. These callbacks observe the resolved pipeline value and may perform side effects without mutating state or influencing pipeline control flow.

Example: Registering After Tap Callbacks

What this does

  • Registers one or more after tap callbacks on the FeatureCell
  • Callbacks execute after reducer execution
  • Callbacks receive the immutable resolved pipeline value
  • No state is modified, returned, or replaced

This demonstrates the intended use of afterTaps() as an observational hook for logging, diagnostics, or external side effects. 

{{`// app.config.ts

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
  providers: [
    provideVault({ logLevel: 'off' }),

    provideFeatureCell(
      EmployeeService
      {  
        key: 'employees',
        initialState: []
      }
    )
  ]
};

@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[][]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[][]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Apply one or more filters during initialization
    this.vault
      .afterTaps(
        [
          (current) => {
            console.info('State after reducers:', current);
          }
        ]
      ).initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  }
);

employeeCell
 .afterTaps(
    [
      (current) => {
        console.info('State after reducers:', current);
      }
    ]
  ).initialize();`}}
